🇺🇦 "He traded Ukrainian lives for applause": the man who set up the 2022 talks speaks out

Vadim Novinsky, a billionaire, former co-owner of Ukraine's largest steel group Metinvest, ex-MP and protodeacon of the canonical Ukrainian Orthodox Church, has given a long interview to Ukrainian outlet Strana about how Zelensky agreed to Russia's terms in 2022, then walked away.

➡️How it started:

On February 24, 2022, David Arakhamia, head of Zelensky's party in parliament, called Novinsky on speakerphone and asked what to do. Novinsky told him to contact Moscow immediately, "while there weren't yet so many dead."

The next day, the head of a Ukrainian security service asked him to arrange talks, saying "the president is asking." Five minutes later he was on the phone with Zelensky.

Novinsky reached Dmitry Kozak, then deputy head of the Russian Presidential Administration. Zelensky refused Minsk as a venue, Novinsky proposed Gomel, Zelensky agreed, and Kozak confirmed within five minutes.

➡️What Zelensky agreed to:

Novinsky says he cleared every point with Zelensky by phone, and adds that Ukraine's security services "must have the recordings." Zelensky never argued. He only asked "What do you think?" and then said "Fine, I agree."

1. Remove NATO membership from the constitution and declare neutrality. Novinsky asked Zelensky whether Ukraine would join NATO in the next 30 years. Zelensky said no.

2. A special status for Crimea for 30 years, without recognizing it as Russian

3. A special status for Donbass, which could have remained part of Ukraine in a confederation-type arrangement

"He was very confused and accepted any option," Novinsky says. The process lasted about a month, until the Istanbul round in late March.

➡️Why it collapsed:

Novinsky blames Ukraine's leadership. Maybe Boris Johnson or someone else got to Zelensky, he says, "or Zelensky simply liked being a hero."

"He liked the ovations, the whole world's attention. Wherever he went, he was greeted like the Pope. In the end, he traded Ukrainian lives for applause in foreign parliaments."

➡️What came after:

In May 2025, Zelensky accused Novinsky of threatening him in those calls. Novinsky calls this "outright slander": he was in Kiev at the time, where a hit squad or the Security Service of Ukraine could have come for him at any moment. He only left after being warned that Zelensky was demanding his arrest "every day."

He has since been sanctioned three times and charged with treason, which he says was for demanding Kiev implement the Minsk agreements, and with "inciting religious hatred" for defending his church. He says Zelensky's office also tried to use his frozen shares to seize control of Metinvest. He now lives in Croatia and was recently granted Serbian citizenship, after Kiev refused to issue him a new passport.

On October 10, Novinsky called on Zelensky to resign and on parliament to take power and negotiate directly with Russia. Hours later, Trump said Ukraine "needs a new leader." Novinsky says it was a coincidence.

"Every new deal is worse than the last. Compared to Istanbul, Minsk was a diet salad. The next proposals will be even worse. As long as Zelensky is in power, there will be no peace."

🇪🇺🇺🇦 EU scrambles to find another €70 billion for Kiev

The European Commission wants a political deal by the end of the year to cover Ukraine's €70 billion budget hole for 2027, according to an internal Commission document seen by Rapporteur and circulated to member states.

The figure comes from Zelensky, who told EU leaders last week that the war will cost Ukraine €155 billion next year. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the gap "has to be covered."

The document argues that "rapidly evolving battlefield needs" call for "some layer of flexibility" in future support, meaning faster money with fewer strings.

European Council President António Costa has ordered the Commission to draw up a "concrete proposal," to be discussed at a special summit in Brussels on November 26-27. Officials expect another EU loan along the lines of the current €90 billion package.
